reconciled 10-11: back to the plan; work continues under the new stories

Q2: Agent proposes `size:` in the investigate stage; founder can override with `card new --size`; a trivial sizing is shown in the local gate note ("size: trivial, skipped research/spec") so Dean sees it once.

Q3: Dogfood on a real one-line fix in codeloop. Given a card sized trivial, when `codeloop run`, then no research.md or spec.md exists, events show create -> build -> verify in one run, and `codeloop stats` shows trivial cycle time under one hour.
Q4: Hard cap: trivial = at most 3 files and 50 changed lines, enforced by `check diff` at verify; over the cap the card is re-sized to S and parked at the spec gate.
Q5: Add `trivial` as a fourth size (one row in the story standard); stages carry `when: size >= S` in build.yaml.

events.note: Q1: Both: a commit is merged when either the local trunk or its remote-tracking branch (the trunk's upstream, else origin) reaches it (accepted the recommendation)
Q2: The trailer wins; the activity record links only commits with no trailer (accepted the recommendation)
Q3: Run it last, in its own commit, only once `git status` shows nothing untracked under specs/; otherwise leave it and say so in the hand-back (accepted the recommendation)

Q4: Run `codeloop orch run --review --dry-run` after the trunk fix and apply what it says for each (close, place or ask); a story it cannot tell about stays where it is, with the reason on the story. (accepted the recommendation)

Q5: A test through the real review pass: a repo whose local main is behind, with a merged commit on origin/main for a story at build, gets the story placed or closed; on the old code it stays put. Then on codeloop's own board `codeloop orch run --review --dry-run` no longer prints the "behind HEAD" warning. (accepted the recommendation)

story.can: start the next story, file a bug, read a story's fields and add an owner decision to it in one command each
story.so: every bug-fix commit names a card and the board matches the work

cards.description: Split from c-362 to keep it within eight tasks; c-362's research.md covers it, so it can start at spec. From the production project's orchestrator board-sync report, 10-18. (a) codeloop start <id> starts a queued or proposed story at its start stage and makes it active in one step; today approve refuses a queued story and says to use card move. (b) codeloop bug "<title>" files a trivial build story flagged as a bug and prints its id for the commit's Card trailer. (c) card show names each blank field (story, description) and the command that fills it; split and queued stories are made with neither (37 of 202 cards on the production board have no story, 60 no description). (d) card edit --description appends a dated owner decision to the description instead of replacing it.
